instruction: Change the system clock format to 24-hour time in the desktop settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing clock format to 24-hour time via desktop settings. Initial config sets clock-format to '12h'. Agent must navigate settings and change to 24-hour format. Evaluator verifies clock-format equals '24h'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts clock-format setting using gsettings command (getter: get_vm_command_line)
Metric (exact_match) appropriately compares command output against expected value using exact string matching
Expected value '24h'\n correctly includes single quotes and newline character that gsettings get command returns
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the single clear requirement - clock format changed to 24-hour time
No UI state dependency - uses command-line verification via gsettings (reads from dconf database), works regardless of UI state
Metric correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' (exact_match receives rules dict and accesses rules['expected'] directly)
Data flow is correct: getter extracts system setting → metric compares → expected value is semantically accurate
Rule validator warning about postconfig for UI state is not applicable here - gsettings reads from system configuration, not UI
